name: Vercel AI SDK generative UI (RSC streamUI, AI SDK UI, @ai-sdk/tui)
tagline: Model tool calls render React components; plus a canned agent TUI

other.label: Migrating from RSC to AI SDK UI

license.notes: LICENSE file is Apache-2.0 (Copyright Vercel); GitHub API reports NOASSERTION.

adoption.summary: The AI SDK is the TypeScript standard for LLM apps; its RSC generative-UI API is a small, experimental corner.

maintainability.release_cadence: Multiple releases per day across packages
maintainability.summary: Very well maintained SDK; RSC module kept but officially experimental.

architecture.summary: AI SDK RSC (@ai-sdk/rsc): streamUI calls a model and lets tools return React Server Components that stream to the client; createStreamableUI/createStreamableValue push UI or values; useUIState/useAIState separate visual state from model context. The docs say RSC is experimental and recommend AI SDK UI (useChat with typed tool parts rendered by client components) for production. @ai-sdk/tui's runAgentTUI runs a ToolLoopAgent (or a remote ChatTransport) in a ready-made terminal chat UI with collapsible tool/reasoning sections and token statistics.
key_points: Generative UI = tool call -> app-defined component; UI is React code, not data
RSC path tied to frameworks supporting React Server Components (Next.js)
runAgentTUI is a fixed chat UI, not a generative or agent-editable surface
No readback, addressing or history of rendered UI

agent_usability.how: The model chooses tools; the app maps tool results to components. runAgentTUI hosts an agent in a terminal chat.
agent_usability.readback: AI state/messages only; the model never sees the rendered UI.
agent_usability.granular_edits: createStreamableUI .update/.append/.done on one streamed node; coarse.
agent_usability.summary: Agent picks components via tools; no live control of the UI.

score_notes.ui_as_data: Components are React code; only tool args/results are data.
score_notes.terminal_native: runAgentTUI renders a fixed chat UI in the terminal; no general terminal renderer.
score_notes.maturity: AI SDK is an ecosystem standard, but RSC generative UI is experimental and discouraged for production.
score_notes.pixel_graphics: Whatever React on the web draws.

steelman: The AI SDK is where most TypeScript LLM apps start (29M weekly downloads), and its generative-UI story is the simplest one there is: let the model call a tool, render a real component for the result, stream it. No new UI language for the model to learn, no catalog DSL, full React and design-system fidelity, type-safe tool parts in useChat, and with @ai-sdk/tui the same agent runs in a polished terminal chat in three lines. For teams that just need 'show a weather card when the model calls getWeather', it is hard to beat.
weaknesses: RSC generative UI is labelled experimental; docs recommend migrating to AI SDK UI
UI is code: no serializable UI, no readback, no patching by id
runAgentTUI is a canned chat interface with display options only
Tied to React (and RSC-capable frameworks for streamUI)

relation_to_scene.overlap: Agents surfacing UI to users; a terminal front end for agents (runAgentTUI).
borrow: runAgentTUI's display modes (full/collapsed/auto-collapsed/hidden) for tool and reasoning sections
ChatTransport abstraction: run local agent or attach to remote one
relation_to_scene.gap_left: Everything scene is about: UI as data, live agent control, readback, patches, data streams, pixels, time travel.
relation_to_scene.verdict_why: Code-first generative UI and a fixed chat TUI; json-render is Vercel's data-first answer and the better comparison.
